items.title: UN Ends Three Decades of Political Mission in Somalia
items.description: The closure of the U.N. Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNTMIS) follows a two-year transition agreed with the federal government. Its responsibilities have been transferred to Somali institutions and U.N. agencies. The mission's roots dates back to 1995, when the U.N. established its Political Office for Somalia. It was replaced by the U.N. Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNSOM) in 2013 before entering its final transition phase as UNTMIS in 2024. items.description: Multiple sources reported fierce clashes in the area, with initial accounts indicating significant losses among federal government forces. items.title: Somalia braces for El Niño floods as millions face risk of hunger
items.description: In Bayahaaw village, on the outskirts of Jowhar in central Somalia, farmers face a difficult choice: plant crops and risk losing them to floodwaters or leave their fields bare and face potential hunger in the coming year. Nuh Adan, a farmer and community leader in Bayahaaw, said flooding caused by breached riverbanks could devastate local agriculture for months. "If the river breaks and the floods hit us, the effects will last until the next rainy season in March," Adan said. items.title: MPS shareholders reject merger with Mediobanca
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, 29 OTT - The shareholders of Monte dei Paschi di Siena (MPS) on Thursday rejected a proposal for the bank to merge with Mediobanca. The proposal needed the support of two-thirds of the bank's capital to be approved, but 63.65% voted against, with only 32.91% in favour and 3.42% abstaining. The merger was part of CEO Luigi Lovaglio's plan to fend off a 33-billion-euro takeover ‌bid by Intesa Sanpaolo for MPS. Intesa Sanpaolo had asked MPS's shareholders to reject the merger, in view of its takeover. MPS took over Mediobanca, Italy's premier merchant bank, earlier this year. Lovag
items.titleIt: MPS shareholders reject merger with Mediobanca

items.description: War has returned to northern Ethiopia, raising fears of a wider conflict involving Eritrea. In this excerpt from the EU Watch List 2026 – Autumn Edition , Crisis Group explains how the EU and member states can facilitate talks and prevent escalation.

items.title: Ethiopia: U.S. Customs Releases Ethiopia-Made Solar Cell Shipments After Supply Chain Review
items.description: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) has released shipments of solar cells manufactured at a Japanese company's facility in Ethiopia following a review of its supply chain documentation, SolarQuarter reported.
items.titleIt: Ethiopia: U.S. Customs Releases Ethiopia-Made Solar Cell Shipments After Supply Chain Review

items.title: Gunfire heard across Ethiopia border as growing numbers flee into Kenya
items.description: Gunfire echoes across the Ethiopia-Kenya border in Moyale, as violence drives thousands to flee into Kenya. The clashes stem from a territorial dispute between Ethiopia’s Oromia and Somali regions.
items.titleIt: Gunfire heard across Ethiopia border as growing numbers flee into Kenya

items.title: Egypt: African Water Facility Launches 2026-2030 Strategy At Cairo Water Week
items.description: [African Development Bank (AfDB)] The African Development Bank Group launched its 2026-2030 African Water Facility Strategy at Cairo Water Week. The launch renews the call for African countries to contribute more resources to water and sanitation projects across the continent. It also calls for private investors to play a greater role in financing these projects.
items.titleIt: Egypt: African Water Facility Launches 2026-2030 Strategy At Cairo Water Week

items.title: Somalia's Eritrean-trained naval chief appointment risks further straining ties with Ethiopia
items.description: Mohamed Abdulqadir "Shariif" has been appointed commander of the Somali Navy and Coastal Defence Forces, replacing Brig. Gen. Abdiwahab Omar. His military training in Eritrea comes at a sensitive time for the region, with relations between Ethiopia and Eritrea deteriorating and renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia raising fears of a wider confrontation.  The appointment could cause concern in Addis Ababa, particularly as Somalia has strengthened its engagement with Eritrea and Egypt amid longstanding disputes with Ethiopia over sovereignty, regional security and access to the Red Sea.
